reviews.comment: Through taking this class you earn a Cultural Discourse and Science credit, so expect some work. I took this during a summer semester (5 weeks) and our workload was 1 quiz, 1 essay, and 1 group meeting per week. It took ONE DAY (~8 hours) to finish an ENTIRE WEEK's worth of work and I ended with a high A and I'm not a STEM major.

Geog 205 is disorganized and needs a lot of restructuring. As it stands, there are recorded group discussions and essays every other week, the latter of which make up 50% of the overall grade and are by themselves 50% peer graded. 25% of your overall grade is left in the hands of your peers. Not a hard class, but still one to steer clear of.
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: The class is a lot of work, but Dr. Jean herself is chill and willing to help if you have questions. She also offers plenty of extra credit on top of fairly light grading, so keeping an A is far from impossible.
The class is a lot of work, but Dr. Jean herself is chill and willing to help you out if you have questions. She also offers plenty of extra credit.

This professor has not gotten this class dialed in AT ALL. She says she inherited the course a few terms ago and is still trying to fix it. Despite being an asynchronous online class, we were required to schedule group meetings via zoom at least biweekly. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS.

Easy online class to get A. Don't expect to do nothing, but also don't think this is going to take much of your time. One essay every other week, one zoom meeting with peers every other week, and a medium amount of reading. Super easy prof to reach online and quick. Very well organized class and Canvas as well. Multiple extra credit opportunities.
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class was the genuine bane of my existence. I dreaded every week, if I could go back in time I would not take it again. The workload is incredibly heavy, and takes far too much time outside of class. The lectures are effectively worthless because you have to read the textbook, so you will sit in class bored out of your mind.

The class is online, but it is organized well and expectations for the course are given upfront. There is an essay every other week that gets graded through peerceptive, so the grading can be a bit confusing. Overall, the course is not very hard, and she gives some extra credit opportunities throughout the semester. Be sure to focus on deadlines!

I honestly do not understand all of these negative comments. I have an easy 100+ in this class. As long as you do the work you'll have an easy A, and its a science course! Sometimes the grading criteria and deadlines were confusing and all over the place, but if you just email her she'll help you!

an easy a just do the work and keep track of deadlines. attendance is semi-mandatory, but i would recommend to just go to class. she gives SO MUCH extra credit. disorganized course and everything written by ai. yeah nobody liked her, you probably wont like her, but you'll like the grade on ur transcript fs !!

This class isn't too bad. One 500-750 word essay every 2 weeks and zoom discussions with preassigned groups make up most of your grade, just make sure to do everything on time. The professor set up the course as a "flipped classroom" which was frustrating but the material isn't hard enough for it to matter that much. It's an average KUCD class.

The class isn't that bad. I took it in person, and I think a lot of people who took it online were expecting an online blow off class. While there is a lot of work it isn't hard and it can get done pretty quickly. The professor is nice, and she's always willing to help. Overall, I'd say like a 3.5/5 because some of the work is just busy work.

This professor was literally everywhere with how she did this course. Quizzes, Essays, and Group Discussions every other week. No perceptiv deadlines in canvas so make sure you keep a heavy eye on it. Nobody I talked to in class liked her because she was everywhere with the course. I wouldn't wish this class upon my worst enemy.

the WORST class ive taken in my educational career. Do NOT take this for an easy core course. You are much better off taking a 300-400 level course for your major. You WILL get flooded with work. For a UCC, I have more assignments and a worse grad than my upper level courses. DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR

For a UCC class, the work load is far too high. The canvas is too chaotic. 2 page essays and group zoom discussions due every two weeks. The extra credit she offers monthly require so much time and effort for so little reward.

DO NOT TAKE HER.

reviews.comment: This class just seemed like a lot of busy work to make up for it being online. We had a quiz, zoom discussion, and essay due every other week with lots of readings. None of the assignments are necessarily hard just time consuming and there's a lot of them. She uses peerceptiv to grade essays. Don't try to email about your grade, she won't change it
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: The work itself in this class is not hard nor time consuming and it's an easy A if you just do it all. Dr. Jean is also so awesome and will work to help you if you talk to her during office hours. There are group discussions and essays, but just do them and you'll be fine. I don't know why everyone is hating on this class, I'd take it again.

There's 6 essays, 6 unit quizzes, 6 zoom discussions, and perceptive reviews over the essays. The class is very manageable and it's easy to get an A, basically if you just do everything. The professor however is pretty unorganized and assignment criteria is oftentimes unclear. Overall pretty easy to succeed but man is it confusing sometimes.

All the graded material comes from quizzes, discussions, essays, and essay reviews which a cycles in that order every 2 weeks. Although the essays aren't very hard, taking this class feels like after one essay is submitted you have the next one breathing down your neck already. Also hate that there's so many steps to each assignment.

This class was not organized very well however it is possible to get an a. It is broken up into units and you have an essay every 2 weeks and then you have group zoom meetings with different groups every two weeks. The class wasn't super hard but TAs did not respond to emails and there is a lot of work for such a basic class. No tests.

Honestly the class wasn't hard. The exams focus on the smallest things that were presented on the slideshows. On the bright side exams are open notes but unless you have all the slideshows with you it is very hard to remember something she breezed over and wrote in the corner of one slide in a 60 slides PowerPoint presentation.

Do not take for an easy online class. Group projects (30 min zoom discussions) every other week which were almost impossible to schedule, and so many essays. The class itself was interesting and the material is not difficult, but coordinating the group projects is not ideal if you are a busy college student.
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: We had to do 30 min discussions every other week about topics having to do with environmental change, and the groups are usually 5+ so you do not talk much. We had essays but they were only 500 words every 2 weeks, and she allows for use of AI but you need to write a statement. The quizzes are easy too. I never read the book or watched lectures.
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Prof Jean's class followed a cycle of two weeks. The first involved reading the course texts and watching lectures, while the second involved group Zoom meetings, taking a quiz, and writing an essay. I wouldn't say the structure was as bad as some may describe, since she makes this two-week assignment schedule known. She also offers extra credit.

This class was a bit tedious. It is easy but time consuming, with essays, group meetings, and biweekly quizzes/peer grading.  I did feel like it was disorganized, but I think she will get better in the future. She seems caring, I missed a group meeting, and she was kind enough to reassign me even though the TA wouldn't. Also, WATCH FOR DUE DATES!

An online class that requires much work. There's an essay due every other week, quizzes, and 30min group discussions. It is tedious to get hold of her and she messed up so many due dates and refused to give another chance to turn it in. Doesn't teach or help with anything, everything is graded by AI or by TA's. DO NOT TAKE HER unless you need to.

Graded off group discussions/assignments, quizzes, and essays. Group discussions must be 30 min. Essay grades depend on peer review, prof simply checks for AI (doesn't read them). Prof doesn't watch group discussions, will give you a 0 if name is not included in submission (even though names are shown in the video). Time consuming and disorganized.

The class is easy to get an A in because of the grading scale and extra credit, but Dr. Jean is incredibly unorganized. I along with many others lost half the points of the first essay because of her lack of communication. Scheduling group zoom sessions is a nightmare, the overall workload is forgettable just very annoying due to poor leadership

This class is easy but there is a big workload. It was very unorganized but my main problem was that the instructions that were given were always so vague. The essay prompts were not very descriptive and the discussion prompts did not give us much to talk about in the 30 minutes we had to talk for. Not hard to get an A with bonus points and effort.

Every assignment except for the exams were actually pretty easy. The problem was, the exams were so difficult and focused on the most specific things from the very long and numerous slideshows we had. The open note aspect only helped if you quite literally had every single piece of material ready. Posted the study guides right before the exam.Avoid

Jean would show up to lectures completely unprepared and did not even know what she was teaching. It felt like she was a random sub pulled in to teach a class. The grading scale magically changed on the day we got our final grades, leaving me with a high B rather than an  A. I am genuinely shocked that she has a PhD; it is INCREDIBLY undeserved.

Not a fan of this class. There were only 2 tests the whole semester, and each one had way too much content packed into it. Even though they were open note, it didn't help much. Lectures were basically just her reading off slides, and she barely explained anything. Wouldn't recommend unless you have to take it.
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The coursework itself is fairly essay but there is just so much of it and the course is set up terribly, I don't think that was her fault though as I think someone else is in charge of that. 7 essays total and group 30 minute discussion which were a pain to schedule since the group changed each time. Most of the material is common sense though.
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: So much content in this class it is ridiculous, but honestly not Dr. Jean's fault. Come to class for the participation points, do all the assignments and quizzes. 2 exams that are open note & really detailed. She offers so much extra credit though (raised my grade by like 5 pts). There are easier science credits though, so maybe take something else

The average for every exam was failing even though they were open note because she makes them so difficult. This was an elective class and harder than my required classes. She doesn't really explain the content either, just goes over slides. Do not take unless you have to

Class is completely asynchronous and online, so the 30 minute group discussions can be really hard to coordinate, especially because the groups switch up every week. Also there is 7 essays, and quizzes, but it's not too bad. Didn't really learn anything, but if you just need the cultural discourse credit then this class should be fine.

She's is such a nice person! But she is not the best prof. She didn't follow her syllabus, and lectures are too much info and hard to follow. Exams are open note, but they honestly don't help all that much unless you directly copy the slides. She is brand new though so that definitely plays a role in the issue.

Class 100% online. Too many students for her to respond to emails when you rlly need her. Lots of essays and zoom, 30 min group discussions every two weeks. No one ever responds and I always had to coordinate every meeting and its difficult to get others to answer. Extra credit is slim. Honestly harder than it needed to be. Don't take this class.
she never came to class, the TA did everything for her

Online, but you have to coordinate 30-minute-long Zoom meetings with several other students every other week, which is hard because of conflicting schedules. I also coordinated every single meeting because other students will contribute nothing to class and rely on others. Essays every other week. Do not take this class.

This class is so unorganized and the professor does not check anything. The actual content is not hard but the way she structures this class makes it unbearable to keep track of. So many freeloaders in my groups that genuinely do not do anything. Way too much group work for an online class it was awful.
So many group project and essay, Strict grading and no extra credits.

reviews.comment: Prof Jeans intro class was super easy and fun. She is very sweet and her lectures are easy to follow. No test only quizzes which are open note and not too hard. Attendance isn't mandatory but she would randomly have a pop quiz that was graded on participation. There is one group project at the end which was pretty easy, would take her again!

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS so frustrating to take and group discussions every other week, half the assignments don't even have due dates on canvas so its hard to keep track of, i know 3 people personally that had to q-drop

I don't know why everyone is hating on this class. lowkey so easy and she is the bomb! Yes, you do have biweekly essays and Zoom calls, but it really is not bad at all. Just plan ahead!! You can write the whole essay in a little over an hour, only 500 words. She responds to emails so quickly and has weekly office hours. I would take it again!!!

Weekly open note online quizzes, Tests were fairly easy as long as you write down the entire powerpoint presentation and key diagrams into your notes (the tests are open note), however it is a lot of content. She does Iclicker, class is very boring but basic material that isn't hard to understand

While I don't have as many issues with this class as other people, I would not recommend it. There are biweekly essays and half hour zoom discussions, which take a lot of time. Also, the essay/discussion topics were hardly on geography - it felt more like a sociology class.
Honestly, this is a very easy class. As long as you keep up with due dates, you will be fine. It is an easy A and doesn't require much work to be put into the class.

There are way too many assignments to keep track of and the due dates don't appear on canvas as the submissions are on another website. You have to calculate your own grade using points. Easy class but don't miss anything on the other website or else you'll have a max 50 for an assignment.

essays are easy to write but there's just so many. If you aren't checking the canvas page every day you can miss an assignment and if you miss one, ur cooked. She was responsive to me and was helpful in her emails. The essay grades were random due to them being given by other students; many used AI but it was allowed so.

The class isn't hard, but it's full of constant busy work. Deadlines come every other day, and it's easy to fall behind. The peer reviews and 30-minute biweekly discussions with random people were the worst part. This class genuinely made me hate working with others, but if you don't mind that and doing meaningless work, this class is for you.

Didn't really see her besides the bi-weekly zoom meetings she would have. Easy class if you do the work early and pay attention to due dates. Only pain is the zoom meetings with randomized groups every other week.

Extremely unresponsive, I'm not entirely sure what exactly she does that gets her paid. Dr. Jean is great, however, the papers are awful. There is one paper every other week graded entirely through Peerceptiv, leaving most of your grade in the course in the hands of other people. She also has quizzes after class, so make sure to stay. HW is also easy.

Her organization is a mess! Due dates are scattered, not in Canvas, so you must check Peerceptive daily. The Canvas dates don't match, and she won't allow makeup. I emailed about my grade and got no response. Her announcements are unclear, making it hard to know what she expects, especially with such odd requirements for an online geography class.

This is the worst and most inconsistent class I have ever taken. It is an absurd amount of work for an online class, and is so unorganized. Every rubric/module you look at will have different requirements that change without telling you. Do not take this class with this professor you will regret it.

I'm in GEOG 205 and I can tell this class gonna be busy work. she just PMO so bad. Her syllabus and the class structure is genuinely all over the place - I understand she's relatively new, but it really does not give excuses as to how terrible the class is structured. So much work for a Language & Phil so please take another course.

Dr. Jean is a great professor. She is nice and her lectures aren't boring. She gives many extra credit opportunities. All quizzes and exams are open note and open slides, which is where most questions are pulled from. There are a few easy assignments and some participation points. Overall, not a hard class and somewhat interesting.

great professor!! i thought her lectures were interesting although she pretty much just read off the slides. her exams are open note and most of the answers are pulled directly from the slides. she had some assignments but they were very straightforward and easy 100s. a lot of extra credit opportunities as well!

I mostly enjoyed Professor Jean's class. It was informational & interesting. My problem is with the organization & grading. This class did not stick to the syllabus, required random check out codes for quizzes, and had many accidental postings and date changes that made me panic each time. If this becomes more organized it would be a great class!
